title: UTF-8 normalization + per-request RNG seed interaction causing eval output drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer (Acme Health) reported sudden regression in evaluation outputs after we rolled runtime-1.21 sampling changes. Symptoms: previously stable evals started over-generating past stop markers and occasionally returned trailing garbled characters for prompts containing non-ASCII stop markers (emoji and ligatures). Initial hypothesis: interaction between new per-request RNG seeding and stop-token matching code path for multibyte/normalized characters. Impact spans Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers that pinned to runtime-1.21. This ticket tracks investigation, diagnosis, fix, tests, rollout and customer communication.
links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4921 - fix: normalize stop-token before match and reorder seed reset
comments: 2026-02-28 | Aisha Patel: Ticket created following Slack escalation from SE; customer provided failing eval examples (emoji stop marker followed by carriage return). Asked for repro and earliest failing runtime. Assigned to Diego.

2026-03-01 | Diego Morales: Reproduced locally against runtime-1.21 with pinned model xglm-30b and customer prompt + stop emoji. Observed two problems: (1) stop matching performed on raw byte sequence, mismatching when prompt had NFKC-equivalent characters, (2) new per-request RNG seeding was applied before finishing stop-token post-processing which changed sampling boundary behavior on edge cases. Both together allowed extra tokens to be emitted.

2026-03-03 | Diego Morales: Added unit tests that exercise multibyte stop tokens (emoji, ligatures, combining diacritics) and deterministic seed placement. Wrote small fuzz harness that mutates normalization forms — failing consistently on raw-match path.

2026-03-05 | Lina Chen (Applied ML): Verified that model logits around stop boundary are sensitive to single-token shifts; seed placement can change whether greedy/beam/truncated sampling hits stop token. Confirms plausible root cause for customer eval drift.

2026-03-07 | Diego Morales: Proposed fix: always normalize stop tokens and input prompt to NFKC at API ingress and perform match in normalized codepoint space; ensure RNG seeding happens after stop detection stage for streaming/early-termination logic. Opened PR #4921 and added regression tests and integration test against emulated customer workload.

2026-03-09 | PM review (Ravi Singh): Approves fix but requests compatibility notes and migration plan for Private customers. Added requirement to avoid changing user-visible tokens — normalization only used for internal matching, not altering user-visible prompt text returned in logs/console.

2026-03-10 | Ops (Mei Park): Ran canary rollout to 3% of Hosted traffic on runtime-1.21. No new errors observed. Acme Health privately validated against their eval harness and reported outputs matched pre-regression baseline for 98/100 seed runs.
2026-03-12 | Security (Omar Farouk): Quick review of KMS usage found no concerns. Security review not required for fix.

2026-03-12 | Diego Morales: Preparing release notes and customer comms. Drafted rollback plan and Private deployment instructions (patch binary + config flag to toggle legacy raw-match for extremely custom setups).

2026-03-12 | Acme Health (customer): Provided additional failing example where stop token included zero-width joiner. Confirmed that the normalization-based matching handles this case in our staging patch. Requested full Dedicated cluster patch and timeline.

2026-03-12 | Diego Morales: Marking ticket In Review. After approval, will merge hotfix to release branch and schedule Dedicated/Private patch windows. Follow-up to update SDK docs describing stop token matching behavior and normalization caveats.
acceptance_criteria: All regression unit tests for multibyte and combining-character stop tokens pass on runtime-1.21.2
Canary rollout shows no increase in generation latency or error rate across Hosted traffic (compare pre-rollout baselines)
Customer-provided eval suites (Acme Health + two other customers) return outputs that match historical golden traces within tolerance
Private and Dedicated deployment docs include clear rollback instructions and a toggle for legacy behavior
Release notes and SDK docs updated to explain internal normalization used for stop matching
rollout_plan: Merge hotfix to release branch and build runtime-1.21.2-b0
Canary: 1% Hosted traffic for 4 hours, monitor token-level deltas and SLOs
If green, ramp to 10% for 12 hours and validate customer eval harnesses
Merge to dedicated/reserved images and schedule Private/Dedicated patch windows during customer-approved maintenance
Post-rollout: monitor dashboards for 72 hours, run nightly golden-eval comparison
postmortem_notes: Root cause: combination of (a) moving seed reset earlier in the request pipeline and (b) stop-token matching operating on raw byte sequences introduced by a prior performance optimization.
Mitigation: normalization at ingress for matching + ensure seed reset ordering preserves semantic stop-detection determinism
Longer-term: add end-to-end evals for stop-token heavy corpora and include normalization fuzzing in CI
Customer comms: apologized, shared timeline and test results, offered Dedicated/Private patch priority
